implemented.frameKeys: WebGL provides the original visual serialization through an explicitly owned key API; its legacy string API remains available. First and comparison keys admit before native serialization. Comparison keys release after consumption. Only a successful stationary frame transfers and retains the first key to the immediately preceding frame cache; replacement releases the previous key. Moving exposures invalidate previous frame keys before accumulation.
implemented.control: Admit the original cache control before construction (192 declared bytes). The actual preview creates it inside existing construction rollback and releases it on final disposal. Its destructor clears root/key/owner references, including allocator disposal before preview disposal.
implemented.failures: Quota denial precedes drawing and preserves the previous frame. A failed draw invalidates the previous framebuffer identity first; original errors, including null, propagate while the new key releases. No cache, moving exposures and unused comparison keys have explicit cleanup. Legacy native string keys and structural comparison preserve original sample/draw counts.
implemented.nativeLifetime: Both actual pinned backends render five stationary frames in forward/reverse/repeated order inside separate frame scratch phases. All pixels match original native output. WebGL performs one original draw and four reuses; Canvas retains its original five draws. Declared metadata current stays constant after every frame and actual preview disposal leaves zero pixel/metadata bytes and reservations. Existing moving/blurred 22 native submission frames and all original real RPC snapshot acknowledgements remain required.
implemented.scope: Selected retained frame key output and cache control. Previous SurfaceNode graphs, damage/vector/provider keys, graph/font and other checksum structures, ledger controls, Node protocol/result copies and actual production/aggregate admission remain pending. Native VM/codec/driver/crypto private storage and RSS are separate.
